chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, through his chain, from some of them (peace be upon them):

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Indeed, the night prayer is more effective in contact [with God] and more suitable for speech [of Quran],' he said: 'It is two rak'ahs after the Maghrib prayer,'

you recite in the first rak'ah - Al-Fatiha and ten verses from the beginning of Al-Baqarah, and the Verse of Al-Sukhr (dominion), from His saying: 'And your god is one God. There is no deity [worthy of worship] except Him, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding' - until His saying: 'For a people who use reason.' And fifteen times 'Say: He is Allah, [who is] One.'

And in the second rak'ah, Al-Fatiha, the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi), and the end of Al-Baqarah from His saying: 'To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth' - until you conclude the surah, and fifteen times 'Say: He is Allah, [who is] One.'
Then supplicate after this with whatever you wish.'
He said: 'And whoever is consistent with it, Allah will record for him, for every prayer, six hundred thousand Hajj [rewards].'

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, [who is] One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific Quranic recitations and rewards for the two-rak'ah prayer after Maghrib?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the specific recitations for the two-rak'ah prayer after Maghrib, often identified with the Prayer of Tasbih, emphasizing the 'Night Prayer' (Na'shi'at al-Layl) as a time of spiritual clarity. It prescribes detailed Quranic selections, including extended passages from Surah Al-Baqarah and repeated recitation of Surah Al-Ikhlas, followed by free supplication, promising a reward of 600,000 Hajj performances for consistent practice. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the merit of night worship and the transformative power of consistent devotion.
